newsitem.title: UK: UN declines comment on Sunday meeting with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: UN declines comment on Sunday meeting with Iraq.

text.p: U.N. officials contacted by telephone in Baghdad declined comment on Monday on the outcome of a meeting yesterday to discuss Iraq's food distribution plan for the second wave of the oil-for-food plan.

Iraqi officials gave the United Nations a preliminary draft plan for aid distribution last Wednesday, which U.N. officials said still needed some work before it can be presented to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
Annan must the plan in order to restart oil exports under the "oil-for-food" scheme which allows Baghdad an exemption to broader sanctions to alleviate suffering of ordinary Iraqis.
Oil exports under the scheme began on December 10 and ran initially for 180 days. The deal was renewed from June 8 but exports have been stalled pending receipt of a new distribution plan.
Iraq's oil minister said two weeks ago that he expected oil exports to begin at a rate of around 730,000 to 750,000 barrels per day (bpd).
